title: Individual-giving decline at Tri-County Harvest Food Bank

organization.size: 34 staff, about 600 regular volunteers, $9.1M annual budget; serves Ashby, Bellmont and Carrow counties

presentingRequest: Individual donations are down 22% this year, and the slide started the month our new executive director, Dana Whitfield, arrived. Major donors tell me she doesn't call them, and our development director quit within six weeks of her starting. The board votes in December on whether to end her contract. We need you to confirm what is driving the decline and help us put the case in front of the board. - Gerald Lindqvist, Board Chair

evidence.text: "Individual giving has collapsed 22% since Dana arrived in March. Ruth Okafor told me at the September volunteer luncheon that she hasn't heard a word from the new director. Our development director, Alicia Moreno, quit about six weeks after Dana started - that tells you everything. People will say it's the economy, but this region has always given, mill or no mill. We had a stable development operation until she took over."

evidence.source: Finance Manager, individual-giving report to the board, Jan-Sep 2026 vs Jan-Sep 2025 (prepared 2026-10-15 from GiveLedger gift records)
evidence.text: Individual donations: 2025 $2,362,000; 2026 $1,841,800 (-22.0%, -$520,200). By channel: monthly recurring (sustainer) gifts $612,000 -> $310,800 (-$301,200); one-time online gifts $540,000 -> $470,000 (-$70,000); direct-mail appeal gifts $690,000 -> $611,000 (-$79,000); major gifts ($5,000+) $520,000 -> $450,000 (-$70,000). Report footnote: 'Figures are gifts recorded in the donor database. Receipts held in the general-ledger suspense account are not included.'

2025-09-18: Board approves migrating the donor database from DonorPoint to GiveLedger; project to be run by the interim executive director (Tom Becker) with the vendor's implementation team; go-live/cutover scheduled for 2026-02-16. 2026-01-22: Board approves hiring Dana Whitfield as executive director; start date 2026-03-02. Interim ED Becker's last day recorded as 2026-03-06.

evidence.source: HR file: development director resignation and 2025 stewardship plan
evidence.text: Development Director Alicia Moreno submitted her resignation on 2026-04-10, effective 2026-05-01; letter states she is relocating to Denver for her spouse's new job. Position vacant since; recruitment paused by the board finance committee on 2026-05-21 'pending budget review'. The 2025 stewardship plan assigned the development director to make quarterly phone calls to the top 50 donors by lifetime giving; no one has been assigned those calls since May 2026.

evidence.source: GiveLedger recurring-gift run log and DonorPoint January-February history (exported 2026-10-20)
evidence.text: Monthly recurring charges attempted / revenue: Jan 2026 (DonorPoint) 1,112 / $68,200; Feb 2026 (DonorPoint) 1,108 / $67,600. Cutover 2026-02-16. First GiveLedger recurring run executed automatically 2026-03-01 06:00 on a schedule configured by the vendor at go-live: 406 charges attempted / $25,300. Apr-Sep 2026: 398-411 charges attempted per month, revenue $24,600-$25,400 per month. Decline rate on attempted charges: 2.9% in Feb (DonorPoint), 3.1% Mar-Sep average (GiveLedger).

evidence.source: Vendor migration completion report, GiveLedger implementation team (dated 2026-02-20)
evidence.text: 1,140 sustainer profiles imported. 438 imported as 'Active' with payment method. 702 imported as 'Pending payment method' because stored card tokens held by the legacy processor CardVault could not be transferred to GiveLedger's processor; GiveLedger does not attempt charges for pending profiles. Recommendation: 'Client should contact affected donors to re-enter payment details.' Note: 'Legacy recurring schedules inside the CardVault merchant account were not modified or cancelled by the vendor; cancellation of legacy schedules is the client's responsibility.' The report does not inventory how many sustainer schedules were stored natively in CardVault (and so may still be running) versus triggered from DonorPoint (which stopped at cutover). Sign-off: T. Becker (interim ED), 2026-02-20. No record of the recommended donor contact being sent exists in GiveLedger's communications log.

"Since March we've been getting monthly bank deposits labelled CV-BATCH from the old CardVault merchant account - $181,300 in total from March through September, between $25,100 and $26,600 each month. I park them in suspense as unidentified receipts. I can't see what's inside them: the only CardVault login belonged to Tom Becker, and he left in March. Historically that account took sustainer gifts, but it also took the 14 corporate Hunger Partner pledges, about $17,500 a month in total, and the Ashby community-kitchen tenant's fees, about $8,000 a month. I don't know whether those partners and the tenant moved to the new GiveLedger forms or to bank transfer - I've been booking corporate and rent revenue from their statements, not matched to deposits. Also, CardVault's terms say transaction history is only viewable on an open account; closed accounts are purged after 30 days."

evidence.source: Donor-services contact log (GiveLedger and DonorPoint), Mar-Sep 2026 vs Mar-Sep 2025
evidence.text: Donor-initiated recurring-gift cancellations: 2025 27; 2026 23. Logged complaints: 2025 19; 2026 47. 2026 complaints by category: 31 'my monthly gift seems to have stopped' or 'my monthly receipts stopped'; 4 objecting to the spring appeal's 'political' or advocacy tone; 12 other (address changes, receipt timing). No complaint in either year names the executive director.

evidence.source: Major-gift detail, Jan-Sep 2025 vs Jan-Sep 2026 (Finance Manager)
evidence.text: 2025: $520,000 from 41 donors, including a one-time $75,000 gift from Harold Brandt (April 2025); Mr. Brandt died on 2025-11-08 and no estate gift has been notified. Excluding Brandt: 2025 $445,000 from 40 donors. 2026: $450,000 from 43 donors. Of the 40 non-Brandt 2025 major donors, 33 had given again by 2026-09-30; in the comparable 2024->2025 period, 32 of 39 had given again by 2025-09-30. 21 of the 33 2026 repeat gifts were received after 2026-05-01.

Gifts: $12,000 on 2025-05-14; $12,000 on 2026-06-09. Contact history 2026: thank-you letter signed by Dana Whitfield 2026-06-12; no phone call or meeting logged in 2026. Contact history 2025: two phone calls logged by the development director.

evidence.source: State Department of Labor county unemployment series and press release
evidence.text: Corwin Paper Mill in Ashby County closed on 2026-01-30 (1,100 jobs). Unemployment, Sep 2025 -> Sep 2026: Ashby County 3.8% -> 6.4%; Bellmont County 3.5% -> 3.9%; Carrow County 3.6% -> 4.0%. Ashby County addresses account for 38% of the food bank's 2025 individual donors. The food bank's own pantry-visit count rose 31% Jan-Sep 2026 vs 2025.

evidence.source: Statewide food-bank network, member giving pulse survey (published 2026-08-28)
evidence.text: Self-reported change in individual giving, Jan-Jun 2026 vs Jan-Jun 2025: 11 of 19 member food banks responded; median -4%, range -17% to +6%. Responses are anonymous and not broken out by region; respondents used their own definitions of 'individual giving'.

evidence.source: Spring direct-mail appeal results, 2025 vs 2026 (GiveLedger campaign report)
evidence.text: 2025 appeal mailed 2025-04-22 to 17,900 households (letter written by the former development director, hunger-relief stories): response rate 7.0%, average gift $57. 2026 appeal mailed 2026-04-20 to 18,400 households (letter rewritten by the executive director, emphasising state SNAP cuts and inviting donors to contact legislators): response rate 6.1%, average gift $58. No split test or control letter was used; results are not broken out by county or donor segment. Fall 2026 appeal not yet mailed.

"In May I saw the monthly recurring numbers fall off a cliff from March and asked the finance committee to pay the auditors to reconcile the old CardVault account. They told me to wait for the January audit. I rewrote the spring letter around the SNAP cuts because pantry visits are up 31% - some donors may not have liked that. I haven't been making the top-donor calls Alicia used to make; I've been covering two warehouse supervisor vacancies since June."

Present: Treasurer (chair of committee), Board Chair, one other director, Finance Manager; ED attending. 'ED requested funds (est. $6,500) to engage the auditors for a reconciliation of the legacy CardVault account and recurring-gift data. Committee deferred the request to the FY2026 audit fieldwork (January 2027).' Same meeting: development director recruitment paused pending budget review.

21 of 34 staff responded. 62% agree 'The executive director communicates a clear direction.' Free-text comments mentioning the ED: three describe her as 'brusque with volunteers', two praise her 'focus on client need'. The survey contains no items about donors or fundraising, and no prior-year survey exists for comparison.

Three-year term from 2026-03-02. Termination without cause by the board requires six months' base salary as severance ($62,500). Section 4: first formal performance review due at 12 months (March 2027); the agreement sets no fundraising targets for 2026.

hypotheses.text: The new executive director is the primary cause of the 22% decline in individual donations (her arrival and conduct account for most of the lost giving).
The executive director's handling of major donors caused the decline in major gifts.
The regional economic downturn following the Corwin Paper Mill closure is the main driver of the decline in one-time online and direct-mail gifts.
Most of the 702 sustainers left in 'Pending payment method' status by the migration have actually stopped giving (their monthly gifts no longer reach the food bank by any route).
More than a quarter of the reported $520,200 decline is a recording gap: money from individual donors is still arriving but is not booked as individual donations.
The executive director's style, including the advocacy-focused spring appeal, contributed to the decline in small-donor (one-time online and direct-mail) giving.

edges.from: February 2026 donor-database migration (702 sustainer profiles imported without a payment method)
edges.to: Drop in recurring-gift revenue recorded in the donor database

edges.from: Regional economic downturn (Ashby County mill closure, rising unemployment)
edges.to: Decline in one-time online and direct-mail gifts

edges.from: Executive director's rewrite of the spring appeal letter around SNAP advocacy
Absence in 2026 of Harold Brandt's one-time 2025 gift (donor deceased)

actions.text: Recommend that the board terminate the executive director at its December meeting on the grounds that she caused the 22% decline in individual donations.

Regain access to the CardVault merchant account through the processor's account-owner verification and reconcile its transaction-level records against the 702 pending sustainer profiles, the corporate Hunger Partner pledges and the kitchen tenant's fees, funding the auditor reconciliation now rather than at the January audit.
Immediately send a mail and phone campaign to all 702 'Pending payment method' sustainers asking them to re-enter their card details in GiveLedger.
Close the legacy CardVault merchant account now to complete the migration and stop the unidentified deposits.
Agree in writing with the executive director who will make the quarterly top-50 donor stewardship calls until the development director post is filled.

evidenceRequests.text: CardVault transaction-level settlement export, March-September 2026, with payer identifiers and schedule IDs
2025 vs 2026 one-time online and spring-appeal giving, split by donor county (Ashby vs Bellmont and Carrow)
Board Chair's written notes of donor conversations at 2026 events
360-degree feedback from staff and volunteers on the executive director's management style
Statewide food-bank network full-year 2026 giving survey (due February 2027)
Telephone check with a random sample of 50 'Pending payment method' sustainers: are monthly charges to the food bank still appearing on their card statements?
